description: Hypercore is a secure, distributed append-only log

sections.title: Features
sections.markdown:
## Features

- **Sparse replication.** Only download the data you are interested in.
- **Realtime.** Get the latest updates to the log fast and securely.
- **Performant.** Uses a simple flat file structure to maximize I/O performance.
- **Secure.** Uses signed merkle trees to verify log integrity in real time.
- **Modular.** Hypercore aims to do one thing and one thing well - distributing a stream of data.

Note that the latest release is Hypercore 10, which adds support for truncate and many other things.
Version 10 is not compatible with earlier versions (9 and earlier), but is considered LTS, meaning the storage format and wire protocol is forward compatible with future versions.

methods.name: constructor

params.name: storage
params.description: `storage` should be set to a directory where you want to store the data and core metadata.

params.name: key
params.description: `key` can be set to a Hypercore key which is a hash of Hypercore's internal auth manifest, describing how to validate the Hypercore.

params.name: opts
params.description: `options` include:

methods.description: Make a new Hypercore instance.

options.name: createIfMissing
options.description: create a new Hypercore key pair if none was present in storage

options.name: overwrite
options.description: overwrite any old Hypercore that might already exist

options.name: force
options.description: Advanced option. Will force overwrite even if the header's key & the passed key don't match

options.name: valueEncoding
options.description: defaults to binary

options.name: encodeBatch
options.description: optionally apply an encoding to complete batches

options.name: keyPair
options.description: optionally pass the public key and secret key as a key pair

options.name: encryption
options.description: the block encryption key

options.name: onwait
options.description: hook that is called if gets are waiting for download

options.name: timeout
options.description: wait at max some milliseconds (0 means no timeout)

options.name: writable
options.description: disable appends and truncates

options.name: inflightRange
options.description: Advanced option. Set to [minInflight, maxInflight] to change the min and max inflight blocks per peer when downloading.

options.name: ongc
options.description: A callback called when the session is garbage collected

options.name: onseq
options.description: A callback called when core.get(index) is called.

options.name: notDownloadingLinger
options.description: How many milliseconds to wait after downloading finishes keeping the connection open. Defaults to a random number between 20-40s

options.name: allowFork
options.description: Enables updating core when it forks

options.name: userData
options.description: An object to assign to the local User Data storage

options.name: manifest
options.description: Advanced option. Set the manifest when creating the hypercore. See Manifest section for more info

options.name: preload
options.description: Advanced option. A promise that returns constructor options overrides before the core is opened

options.name: storage
options.description: An alternative to passing storage as a dedicated argument

options.name: key
options.description: An alternative to passing key as a dedicated argument

examples: const core = new Hypercore('./directory') // store data in ./directory

{
  createIfMissing: true, // create a new Hypercore key pair if none was present in storage
  overwrite: false, // overwrite any old Hypercore that might already exist
  force: false, // Advanced option. Will force overwrite even if the header's key & the passed key don't match
  valueEncoding: 'json' | 'utf-8' | 'binary', // defaults to binary
  encodeBatch: batch => { ... }, // optionally apply an encoding to complete batches
  keyPair: kp, // optionally pass the public key and secret key as a key pair
  encryption: { key: buffer }, // the block encryption key
  onwait: () => {}, // hook that is called if gets are waiting for download
  timeout: 0, // wait at max some milliseconds (0 means no timeout)
  writable: true, // disable appends and truncates
  inflightRange: null, // Advanced option. Set to [minInflight, maxInflight] to change the min and max inflight blocks per peer when downloading.
  ongc: (session) => { ... }, // A callback called when the session is garbage collected
  onseq: (index, core) => { ... }, // A callback called when core.get(index) is called.
  notDownloadingLinger: 20000, // How many milliseconds to wait after downloading finishes keeping the connection open. Defaults to a random number between 20-40s
  allowFork: true, // Enables updating core when it forks
  userData: { foo: 'bar' }, // An object to assign to the local User Data storage
  manifest: undefined, // Advanced option. Set the manifest when creating the hypercore. See Manifest section for more info
  preload: undefined, // Advanced option. A promise that returns constructor options overrides before the core is opened
  storage: undefined, // An alternative to passing storage as a dedicated argument
  key: null, // An alternative to passing key as a dedicated argument
}

{
  version: 1,                       // Version of the manifest format
  hash: 'blake2b',                  // Only Blake2b is supported currently
  allowPatch: false,                // Whether the hypercore can be "patched" to change the signers
  quorum: (signers.length / 2) + 1, // How many signers needed to verify a block
  signers,                          // Array of signers for the core
  prologue: null,                   // The tree hash and length of the core
  linked: null,                     // Array of associated core keys. Only supported in versions >= 2
  userData: null                    // Arbitrary buffer for User Data integral to the core. Only supported in versions >= 2
}

methods.name: MAX_SUGGESTED_BLOCK_SIZE
methods.description: The constant for max size (15MB) for blocks appended to Hypercore. This max ensures blocks are replicated smoothly.

params.name: manifest

params.name: options
params.description: `options` include:

methods.returns: Returns the key for a given manifest.
methods.description: `options` include:

options.name: compat

options.name: version

methods.name: discoveryKey

params.name: key
params.description: The 32-byte Hypercore public key.

methods.returns: Returns the discovery key for the provided `key`.
methods.description:
Derive the discovery key from a Hypercore public key. The discovery key
can safely be shared to announce the core without exposing the read key.
examples: const dKey = Hypercore.discoveryKey(core.key)

methods.name: blockEncryptionKey

params.name: key
params.description: The 32-byte Hypercore public key.

params.name: encryptionKey
params.description: The 32-byte master encryption key.

methods.returns: Returns a block encryption key derived from the `key` and `encryptionKey`.
methods.description:
Derive a block-level encryption key from the Hypercore public key and a
master encryption key using BLAKE2b.
examples: const blockKey = Hypercore.blockEncryptionKey(core.key, encryptionKey)

methods.name: getProtocolMuxer

params.name: stream
params.description: A Hypercore protocol stream (as returned by `core.replicate()` or `Hypercore.createProtocolStream()`).

methods.returns: Returns a protomux instance from the provided `stream` Hypercore protocol stream.
methods.description: Extract the Protomux instance attached to a Hypercore protocol stream.
examples:
const stream = core.replicate(true)
const mux = Hypercore.getProtocolMuxer(stream)

methods.name: createCore

params.name: storage
params.description: Path to a storage directory, or a CoreStorage instance.

params.name: opts
params.description: Options forwarded to the Core constructor.

methods.returns: Returns the internal core using the `storage` and `opts` without creating a full Hypercore instance.
methods.description:
Create the raw internal Core object directly, bypassing the Hypercore
session layer. Useful for low-level tooling that needs direct storage access.
examples: const core = Hypercore.createCore('./storage', { key: myKey })

methods.name: createProtocolStream

params.name: isInitiator
params.description: `isInitiator` can be a framed stream, a protomux or a boolean for whether the stream should be the initiator in the noise handshake.

params.name: opts
params.description: `opts` can include:

methods.returns: The outer raw stream with a `.noiseStream.userData` Protomux attached.
methods.description: Create an encrypted noise stream with a protomux instance attached used for Hypercore's replication protocol.

options.name: ondiscoverykey
options.description: A handler for when a discovery key is set over the stream for corestore management

methods.name: defaultStorage

params.name: storage
params.description: Directory path string or an existing CoreStorage instance (returned as-is).

params.name: opts
params.description: Extra options forwarded to the CoreStorage constructor.

methods.returns: Returns a default hypercore storage.
methods.description:
Wrap a path or existing CoreStorage object into a CoreStorage instance.
Called internally by the constructor; exposed for advanced use.
examples: const storage = Hypercore.defaultStorage('./my-core')

methods.name: snapshot

params.name: opts
params.description: Options forwarded to `core.session()` with `snapshot: true` set automatically.

methods.returns: A new read-only Hypercore session locked to the current length.
methods.description: Same as [`core.session(options)`](#const-session--coresessionoptions), but backed by a storage snapshot so will not truncate nor append.
examples:
const snap = core.snapshot()
console.log(snap.length) // frozen at the moment snapshot() was called

methods.name: session

params.name: opts
params.description: Options are inherited from the parent instance, unless they are re-set.

methods.returns: A new Hypercore session sharing the same underlying storage.
methods.description: Creates a new Hypercore instance that shares the same underlying core.

options.name: weak
options.description: Creates the session as a "weak ref" which closes when all non-weak sessions are closed

options.name: exclusive
options.description: Create a session with exclusive access to the core. Creating an exclusive session on a core with other exclusive sessions, will wait for the session with access to close before the next exclusive session is `ready`

options.name: checkout
options.description: A index to checkout the core at. Checkout sessions must be an atom or a named session

options.name: atom
options.description: A storage atom for making atomic batch changes across hypercores

options.name: name
options.description: Name the session creating a persisted branch of the core. Still beta so may break in the future

examples:
{
  weak: false // Creates the session as a "weak ref" which closes when all non-weak sessions are closed
  exclusive: false, // Create a session with exclusive access to the core. Creating an exclusive session on a core with other exclusive sessions, will wait for the session with access to close before the next exclusive session is `ready`
  checkout: undefined, // A index to checkout the core at. Checkout sessions must be an atom or a named session
  atom: undefined, // A storage atom for making atomic batch changes across hypercores
  name: null, // Name the session creating a persisted branch of the core. Still beta so may break in the future
}

methods.name: setEncryptionKey

params.name: key
params.description: The 32-byte encryption key to use for block encryption/decryption.

params.name: opts
params.description: `opts` includes:

methods.returns: Resolves once the encryption provider has been installed.
methods.description: Set the encryption key.

options.name: block
options.description: Whether the key is for block encryption

methods.name: setEncryption

params.name: encryption
params.description: An encryption provider with `padding`, `encrypt`, and `decrypt` methods, or `null` to disable encryption.

methods.returns: Resolves once the encryption provider has been installed.
methods.description: Set the encryption, which should satisfy the [HypercoreEncryption](https://github.com/holepunchto/hypercore-encryption) interface.
examples: await core.setEncryption(new DefaultEncryption(encryptionKey, core.key))

methods.name: setGroup

params.name: topic
params.description: `topic` is a 32 byte buffer.

methods.description: Set the group `topic` that the hypercore belongs to. Useful for grouping hypercores together that need to update a larger data structure (eg. `autobee`) that is comprised of them. See `corestore`'s `store.notifyGroup(topic)` for more details.

methods.name: setKeyPair

params.name: keyPair
params.description: The new Ed25519 key pair to use for signing.

methods.description: Update the core's `keyPair`. Advanced as the `keyPair` is used throughout Hypercore, e.g. verifying blocks, identifying the core, etc.
examples: core.setKeyPair({ publicKey: pubKey, secretKey: secKey })

methods.name: setActive

params.name: bool
params.description: Pass `true` to mark the core as active, `false` to deactivate.

methods.description: Set the core to be active or not. A core is considered 'active' if it should linger to download blocks from peers.
examples: core.setActive(false) // stop lingering for peer downloads

methods.name: close

params.name: options
params.description: Optional close options.

methods.returns: Resolves once the session (and underlying core if no other sessions remain) is fully closed.
methods.description: Fully close this core. Passing an error via `{ error }` is optional and all pending replicator requests will be rejected with the error.
examples: await core.close()

methods.name: commit
methods.signature: const { byteLength, length } = await core.commit(session, opts = {})

params.name: session
params.description: The named or atom session whose staged blocks should be committed.

params.name: opts
params.description: `opts` includes:

methods.returns: Returns `null` if committing failed.
methods.description: Attempt to apply blocks from the session to the `core`. `core` must be a default core, aka a non-named session.

options.name: length
options.description: the core's length after committing the blocks

options.name: treeLength
options.description: The expected length of the core's merkle tree prior to commit

options.name: keyPair
options.description: The keypair to use when committing

options.name: signature
options.description: The signature for the blocks being committed

methods.name: replicate

params.name: isInitiator
params.description: `true`/`false` for the noise handshake role, or an existing stream / Protomux to attach to.

params.name: opts
params.description: `opts` are same as [`Hypercore.createProtocolStream()`](#const-stream--hypercorecreateprotocolstreamisinitiator-opts--).

methods.returns: The replication stream (a raw duplex stream with a Protomux attached).
methods.description: Create a replication stream. You should pipe this to another Hypercore instance.

methods.name: id
methods.returns: The z-base-32 encoded public key, or `null` before the core is opened.
methods.description: String containing the id (z-base-32 of the public key) identifying this core.

methods.name: key
methods.returns: The 32-byte public key, or `null` before the core is opened.
methods.description: Buffer containing the public key identifying this core.

methods.name: discoveryKey
methods.returns: The 32-byte discovery key, or `null` before the core is opened.
methods.description: Buffer containing a key derived from the core's public key. In contrast to `core.key` this key does not allow you to verify the data but can be used to announce or look for peers that are sharing the same core, without leaking the core key.

methods.name: length
methods.returns: The total number of blocks in the core (0 before the core is opened).
methods.description: How many blocks of data are available on this core.

methods.name: signedLength
methods.returns: The number of quorum-signed blocks (0 before the core is opened).
methods.description: How many blocks of data are available on this core that have been signed by a quorum. This is equal to `core.length` for Hypercores with a single signer.

methods.name: byteLength
methods.description: Deprecated. Use `const { byteLength } = await core.info()`.

methods.name: remoteContiguousLength
methods.returns: The remote contiguous length (0 before the core is opened).
methods.description: How many blocks are contiguously available starting from the first block of this core on any known remote. This is only updated when a remote thinks it is fully contiguous such that they have all known blocks.

methods.name: contiguousLength
methods.returns: The local contiguous length (0 before the core is opened).
methods.description: How many blocks are contiguously available starting from the first block of this core.

methods.name: fork
methods.returns: The current fork counter (incremented on each truncation; 0 before the core is opened).
methods.description: What is the current fork id of this core?

methods.name: padding
methods.returns: Number of padding bytes prepended to each block (0 when encryption is disabled).
methods.description: How much padding is applied to each block of this core? Will be `0` unless block encryption is enabled.

methods.name: peers
methods.returns: Live array of Replicator peer objects (empty before the core is opened).
methods.description: Array of current peers the core is replicating with.

methods.name: ready
methods.returns: Resolves once the core is ready for reading and writing.
methods.description: Wait for the core to fully open.

methods.name: setUserData

params.name: key
params.description: `key` is a string and `value` can be a string or buffer.

params.name: value
params.description: The value to store (Buffer or UTF-8 string).

methods.returns: Resolves once the value has been persisted to storage.
methods.description: Set a key in the User Data key-value store.
examples: await core.setUserData('version', Buffer.from('1.0'))

methods.name: getUserData

params.name: key
params.description: `key` is a string.

methods.returns: Return the value for a key in the User Data key-value store.
methods.description: `key` is a string.
examples:
const value = await core.getUserData('version')
console.log(value && value.toString()) // '1.0'

methods.name: findingPeers
methods.returns: A `done()` callback to call when peer discovery is complete.
methods.description: Create a hook that tells Hypercore you are finding peers for this core in the background. Call `done` when your current discovery iteration is done. If you're using Hyperswarm, you'd normally call this after a `swarm.flush()` finishes.
examples:
const done = core.findingPeers()
swarm.flush().then(done, done)

methods.name: info

params.name: opts
params.description: `options` include:

methods.returns: An `Info` object with `key`, `discoveryKey`, `length`, `contiguousLength`, `byteLength`, `fork`, `padding`, and optional `storage` fields.
methods.description: Get information about this core, such as its total size in bytes.

options.name: storage
options.description: get storage estimates in bytes, disabled by default

examples:
Info {
  key: Buffer(...),
  discoveryKey: Buffer(...),
  length: 18,
  contiguousLength: 16,
  byteLength: 742,
  fork: 0,
  padding: 8,
  storage: {
    oplog: 8192,
    tree: 4096,
    blocks: 4096,
    bitfield: 4096
  }
}

methods.name: update

params.name: opts
params.description: `options` include:

methods.returns: `true` if the core was updated to a new length, `false` otherwise.
methods.description: Waits for initial proof of the new core length until all `findingPeers` calls have finished.

options.name: activeRequests
options.description: Advanced option. Pass requests for replicating blocks

options.name: force
options.description: Force an update even if core is writable.

examples:
const updated = await core.update()

console.log('core was updated?', updated, 'length is', core.length)

methods.name: seek

params.name: bytes
params.description: The byte offset to seek to (zero-based).

params.name: opts
params.description: Options controlling wait and timeout behaviour.

methods.returns: Returns `[index, relativeOffset]`, where `index` is the data block the `byteOffset` is contained in and `relativeOffset` is the relative byte offset in the data block.
methods.description: Seek to a byte offset.

options.name: wait
options.description: wait for data to be downloaded

options.name: timeout
options.description: wait at max some milliseconds (0 means no timeout)

options.name: activeRequests
options.description: Advanced option. Pass requests for replicating blocks

examples:
await core.append([Buffer.from('abc'), Buffer.from('d'), Buffer.from('efg')])

const first = await core.seek(1) // returns [0, 1]
const second = await core.seek(3) // returns [1, 0]
const third = await core.seek(5) // returns [2, 1]

methods.name: has

params.name: start
params.description: Zero-based index of the first block to check.

params.name: end
params.description: Exclusive end index (defaults to `start + 1`, i.e. checks a single block).

methods.returns: `true` if every block in `[start, end)` is available locally.
methods.description: Check if the core has all blocks between `start` and `end`.
examples:
const hasBlock = await core.has(5)
const hasRange = await core.has(0, 10)

methods.name: get

params.name: index
params.description: Zero-based index of the block to retrieve.

params.name: opts
params.description: `options` include:

methods.returns: The block value (decoded per `valueEncoding`), or `null` if the block is not available and `wait` is `false`.
methods.description: Get a block of data. If the data is not available locally this method will prioritize and wait for the data to be downloaded.

options.name: wait
options.description: wait for block to be downloaded

options.name: onwait
options.description: hook that is called if the get is waiting for download

options.name: timeout
options.description: wait at max some milliseconds (0 means no timeout)

options.name: activeRequests
options.description: Advanced option. Pass BlockRequest for replicating the block

options.name: valueEncoding
options.description: defaults to the core's valueEncoding

options.name: decrypt
options.description: automatically decrypts the block if encrypted

options.name: raw
options.description: Return block without decoding

examples:
{
  wait: true, // wait for block to be downloaded
  onwait: () => {}, // hook that is called if the get is waiting for download
  timeout: 0, // wait at max some milliseconds (0 means no timeout)
  activeRequests: undefined, // Advanced option. Pass BlockRequest for replicating the block
  valueEncoding: 'json' | 'utf-8' | 'binary', // defaults to the core's valueEncoding
  decrypt: true, // automatically decrypts the block if encrypted
  raw: false, // Return block without decoding
}

methods.name: clear

params.name: start
params.description: Zero-based index of the first block to clear.

params.name: end
params.description: Exclusive end index (defaults to `start + 1`).

params.name: opts
params.description: `options` include:

methods.returns: `{ blocks }` with the count of cleared blocks when `opts.diff` is true, otherwise `null`.
methods.description: Clear stored blocks between `start` and `end`, reclaiming storage when possible.

options.name: diff
options.description: Returned `cleared` bytes object is null unless you enable this

examples:
await core.clear(4) // clear block 4 from your local cache
await core.clear(0, 10) // clear block 0-10 from your local cache

methods.name: markBlock

params.name: start
params.description: Zero-based index of the first block to mark.

params.name: end
params.description: `end` is non-inclusive and defaults to `start + 1` so `core.markBlock(index)` only marks the block at `index`.

methods.returns: Resolves once all marks in the range have been written to storage.
methods.description: Manually mark a block or range of blocks to be retained when sweeping. Useful to mark blocks without loading them into memory. `end` is non-inclusive and defaults to `start + 1` so `core.markBlock(index)` only marks the block at `index`.
examples:
await core.markBlock(5)       // mark block 5
await core.markBlock(0, 10)   // mark blocks 0–9

methods.name: clearMarkings
methods.returns: Resolves once all marks have been cleared from storage.
methods.description: Manually remove all markings. Automatically called when calling `core.startMarking()`.
examples: await core.clearMarkings()

methods.name: startMarking
methods.returns: Resolves once marking mode is active and previous marks are cleared.
methods.description: This enables marking mode for the "mark & sweep" approach to clear hypercore storage. When called the current markings are cleared.
examples:
await core.startMarking()
await core.get(2)
await core.get(4)
await core.sweep() // All blocks but blocks 2 & 4 are cleared

methods.name: sweep

params.name: options
params.description: `opts` can include:

methods.returns: Resolves once all unmarked blocks have been cleared.
methods.description: Clear all unmarked blocks from storage.

options.name: batchSize
options.description: How frequently to flush clears to storage.

methods.name: createReadStream

params.name: opts
params.description: `options` include:

methods.returns: A Readable stream that emits decoded blocks.

options.name: wait

options.name: timeout

options.name: live

methods.name: createWriteStream

methods.name: createByteStream

params.name: opts
params.description: `options` include:

methods.returns: A Readable stream that emits raw Buffer chunks spanning the requested byte range.
methods.description: Make a byte stream to read a range of bytes.

options.name: byteOffset

options.name: prefetch
options.description: How many bytes to download at a time

methods.name: download

params.name: range
params.description: The block range to download. Omit to download the entire core.

methods.returns: A Download handle with a `.done()` promise and a `.destroy()` method to cancel.
methods.description: Download a range of data.

params.name: newLength
params.description: =0] - The target length to truncate to (must be ≤ current `core.length`).

params.name: opts
params.description: `options` include:

methods.returns: Resolves once the truncation has been signed and written to storage.
methods.description: Truncate the core to a smaller length.

options.name: fork

methods.name: append
methods.signature: const { length, byteLength } = await core.append(block, options = {})

params.name: blocks
params.description: A single block, or an array of blocks, to append.

params.name: opts
params.description: `options` include:

methods.returns: The new `length` and `byteLength` of the core after appending.
methods.description: Append a block of data (or an array of blocks) to the core. Returns the new length and byte length of the core.

methods.name: signable

params.name: length
params.description: The length to sign for (defaults to `core.length`).

params.name: fork
params.description: The fork ID to include (defaults to `core.fork`).

methods.returns: Return a buffer which encodes the core's `key`, tree hash (`core.treeHash()`), `length`, & `fork`.
methods.description:
Produce the signable payload for a given tree state. The payload encodes the
core's `key`, tree hash (`core.treeHash()`), `length`, and `fork`.
examples:
const payload = await core.signable()
const sig = sodium.crypto_sign_detached(payload, secretKey)

methods.name: treeHash

params.name: length
params.description: Tree length to hash at (defaults to `core.length`).

methods.returns: A 32-byte BLAKE2b hash of the Merkle tree roots at the given length.
methods.description: Get the Merkle Tree hash of the core at a given length, defaulting to the current length of the core.
examples:
const hash = await core.treeHash()

methods.name: proof

params.name: opts
params.description: `opts` include:

methods.returns: A settled `TreeProof` object that can be serialised and sent to a remote peer.
methods.description: Generate a proof (a `TreeProof` instance) for the request `opts`.

options.name: block
options.description: Block request

options.name: hash

options.name: seek
options.description: Seek Request

options.name: upgrade

methods.name: verifyFullyRemote

params.name: proof
